why:
Deliberate, and the first substantive thing the contract changes rather than moves. The frozen order — Screens, Layout, Lists, Actions, Selection, Containment, Communication, Content, Embedded — is a taxonomy this repository invented for a catalog whose components it has never compiled; 'Lists', 'Content' and 'Embedded' are not words wear-m3-catalog uses about itself. The policy states that catalog's own @file:CatalogGroup(section = ...) vocabulary instead, which is the same vocabulary its published sticker sheet is already organised by, so the builder's insert panel and the catalog's own site stop disagreeing about what a component is filed under. Expect the shelves to move at cutover; that is the change, not a regression.

RE-PINNED 2026-09-12, and the re-pin is this entry's mechanism working rather than failing. The value recorded here was Layout, Navigation, Actions, Selection, Text, Containment, Communication, Motion, Styles, Horologist — ten shelves the catalog had ALSO stopped using. Its own policy says so: 72 of 76 components named a group that list omitted, so the fallback sorted them after nine EMPTY shelves. wear-m3-catalog#455 replaced the list with the twenty-one groups its components actually carry, and the value below is now what BOTH sides state — the authored `ui-builder.policy.json` and the published `ui-builder.json` agree on it exactly. Because this entry pins the policy value and not just the field name, the gate reported it as an unusable exemption the moment the catalog moved instead of waving the change through, which is the whole point of pinning both sides. RE-PINNED again: `Embedded` is gone from the frozen side. It was the shelf holding the three Remote Compose seams, which were offered on Wear without being exportable — the whole-screen generator has no case for any of them — so both the seams and their shelf were withdrawn until that has an answer. An empty shelf is a heading an author opens for nothing. The shelf and its entry here come back when the seams do.

The frozen catalog carries no platformLabel at all — the synthesised Wear catalog was never asked for one, and the builder derives a label from the platform word today. 'Wear' is what the catalog calls itself and what its own published sticker sheet is titled, so it is the string a person recognises. Nothing here can check it; this entry is somebody having read it.

IT WAS NOT ALWAYS THIS ORDINARY, and the history is the point. When first reviewed this entry recorded a SUBSTITUTION: `wear-m3/edge-button` resolved to `androidx.wear.compose.material3.AlertDialogDefaults.EdgeButton` — the button AlertDialog owns — and shelved on `Dialogs`, while the standalone `EdgeButton` that `EdgeButtons.kt` declares was reachable under no id at all. Two components published under one id, with the wrong one winning because AlertDialog sorts first alphabetically among the stickers that draw it.

wear-m3-catalog#474 fixed that at source by pinning the record in `ui-builder.policy.json`, so the id now binds to `EdgeButtonKt.EdgeButton` and sits on its own shelf. This entry was re-pinned rather than deleted because a real difference survives the fix — the lost `size` variant control. Recording the substitution here instead of fixing the catalog would have frozen a collision as deliberate; that is what the pinned-both-sides design is for, and it is what forced the question.

ACCEPTED AS A KNOWN-WRONG SHELF, pinned so it cannot drift further unnoticed. `AppScaffold` is a Wear Material 3 component; `Fast scrolling` is a **Horologist**-section shelf declared by `catalog/src/androidMain/kotlin/ee/schimke/wearm3catalog/sections/FastScrolling.kt`, which does not reference `AppScaffold` anywhere. This is the shelf-collision mechanism, not intent: `@file:CatalogGroup` is file-level, so a library symbol drawn by several stickers takes the shelf of whichever sticker sorts first, and `FastScrollingList` draws this one indirectly through `ScreenSticker`. The corroboration is that the excluded `wear-m3/screen-sticker` landed on the same shelf by the same route. Same class as `circular-progress-indicator` on `Buttons` and `edge-button` bound to AlertDialog's overload, both fixed upstream in wear-m3-catalog#474 rather than recorded here. Recorded rather than fixed this time because the cutover should not wait on an upstream round-trip, and a recorded wrong shelf is visible where an unreviewed one is not. The fix belongs in the catalog; when it lands this entry should be DELETED, not amended, and the gate will say so by failing on the moved shelf.

ACCEPTED AS A KNOWN-WRONG SHELF, pinned so it cannot drift further unnoticed. `TimeText` is a Wear Material 3 component; `Fast scrolling` is a **Horologist**-section shelf declared by `catalog/src/androidMain/kotlin/ee/schimke/wearm3catalog/sections/FastScrolling.kt`, which does not reference `TimeText` anywhere. This is the shelf-collision mechanism, not intent: `@file:CatalogGroup` is file-level, so a library symbol drawn by several stickers takes the shelf of whichever sticker sorts first, and `FastScrollingList` draws this one indirectly through `ScreenSticker`. The corroboration is that the excluded `wear-m3/screen-sticker` landed on the same shelf by the same route. Same class as `circular-progress-indicator` on `Buttons` and `edge-button` bound to AlertDialog's overload, both fixed upstream in wear-m3-catalog#474 rather than recorded here. Recorded rather than fixed this time because the cutover should not wait on an upstream round-trip, and a recorded wrong shelf is visible where an unreviewed one is not. The fix belongs in the catalog; when it lands this entry should be DELETED, not amended, and the gate will say so by failing on the moved shelf.

Deliberate, and ahead of the catalogs rather than behind them. `secondary` / `onSecondary` joined the token vocabulary the canvas draws and both reducers accept, so a design can recolour a Wear button the way ComposeStarter's settings button is recoloured upstream (`IconButtonDefaults.filledIconButtonColors(containerColor = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.secondary, …)`). The roles are one shared list mirrored in PropertyValueKinds, the runtime and the renderer, so every catalog's frozen side gains them at once. The published side is captured from the catalog repositories and still lists the fourteen roles it was captured with; nothing a design names from the old list stops resolving. The entry fails, as intended, when a re-capture carries the two roles, and is deleted then.
